items.explanation: The traditional Valencian version uses chicken, rabbit, green beans and butter beans rather than seafood, and cooks prize the crisp, toasted rice at the bottom, called socarrat.
items.stem: Paella, cooked in a wide, shallow pan, comes from which region of Spain?

items.explanation: In Sri Lanka, growers cut the trees back so they sprout thin shoots, then peel the inner bark from these by hand; it curls into rolls called quills as it dries.
items.stem: Which part of a tree is dried to make cinnamon?

items.explanation: A botanical berry grows from a single flower's ovary, as grapes, tomatoes, chillies and bananas do. A strawberry is a swollen flower base, and each pip on its skin is a tiny fruit.
items.stem: Botanically, bananas are berries, unlike strawberries.

items.explanation: Kneading lines gluten strands up into an elastic web that traps gas from the yeast. Rye flour forms a weak gluten network and rice flour none, so their breads rise less.
items.stem: Which protein network, formed when wheat flour meets water, gives bread dough its stretch?

items.explanation: Even a mild habanero is many times hotter than a fiery jalapeño. The Scoville scale began as a taste test, diluting chilli extract until a panel of tasters felt no heat.
items.stem: Which chilli is hotter?

items.explanation: Burro is Spanish for donkey and -ito makes it small. Nobody knows for sure why; one idea is that the bulging wrap looked like the packs donkeys carried.
items.stem: Which Mexican dish's name means 'little donkey' in Spanish?

items.explanation: Birds feel no burn from capsaicin, so they eat chillies and scatter the seeds unharmed, while mammals, whose teeth would crush the seeds, are put off.
items.stem: Which compound makes chilli peppers taste hot?

items.explanation: Pistachios and poison ivy are in the family too. Cashew shells and mango skin contain irritants related to poison ivy's, which is why cashews are sold shelled.
items.stem: Which of these belongs to the same plant family as the cashew?

items.explanation: The tall lid catches rising steam, which condenses and runs back down, so the stew stays moist and tender with little added liquid.
items.stem: Which North African stew shares its name with the cone-lidded clay pot it is cooked in?

items.explanation: His short-stemmed, disease-resistant wheat sharply raised harvests in Mexico and South Asia, part of the shift in farming known as the Green Revolution.
items.stem: Norman Borlaug won the 1970 Nobel Peace Prize for his work breeding high-yield varieties of which crop?

items.explanation: Tests show seared meat loses as much moisture as unseared meat, or more. What searing does do is brown the surface, creating rich flavours through the Maillard reaction.
items.stem: Searing meat over high heat seals in its juices.

items.explanation: Vanilla is native to Mexico and Central America. Elsewhere growers pollinate each flower by hand, using a method found on Réunion by Edmond Albius, an enslaved boy.
items.stem: Vanilla comes from the cured seed pods of which kind of plant?

items.explanation: Traces of copper bind to a protein in the whites, making the foam more stable. Cooks without copper add a pinch of cream of tartar, an acid, for a similar effect.
items.stem: Whisking egg whites in a bowl made of which metal helps the foam hold its shape?

items.explanation: Charred crumbs from a hearth at Shubayqa in Jordan show hunter-gatherers baking flatbread from wild cereals thousands of years before wheat was domesticated.
items.stem: Which came first?

items.explanation: Chickpeas are also called garbanzo beans. In Egypt, falafel is usually made with fava (broad) beans, while across the Levant it is made with chickpeas.
items.stem: Which legume is the main ingredient of hummus?

items.explanation: Ikeda traced the savoury taste to glutamate in the seaweed and went on to patent monosodium glutamate, or MSG, as a seasoning.
items.stem: Which basic taste did Japanese chemist Kikunae Ikeda identify and name after studying kombu broth?

items.explanation: The colour comes from pigments called betalains, and beetroot (beet) extract is used as a natural red food colouring. In some people, eating beetroot tints urine pink, a harmless effect.
items.stem: Which vegetable gives the soup borscht its deep red colour?

items.explanation: The small domes are pressed with a thumb and come from Puglia in southern Italy. Farfalle means butterflies, linguine little tongues and vermicelli little worms.
items.stem: Which pasta's Italian name means 'little ears'?

items.explanation: Turmeric is a rhizome of the ginger family, boiled and dried before grinding. Its yellow pigment, curcumin, turns red in alkaline conditions, so a turmeric stain goes red when washed with soap.
items.stem: Which spice gives curry powder its bright yellow colour?

items.explanation: Pineapple contains bromelain, an enzyme that breaks down gelatin's proteins. Tinned (canned) pineapple works fine, because heating destroys the enzyme. Fresh kiwifruit and papaya cause the same problem.
items.stem: Fresh pineapple can stop a jelly (gelatin dessert) from setting.

items.explanation: Choux dough is cooked in a pan before baking. In the oven its water turns to steam and inflates each piece, leaving a hollow shell to fill with cream.
items.stem: Which pastry is used to make éclairs and profiteroles?

items.explanation: Nigeria, Ghana, Senegal and their neighbours all have proud versions, and the friendly rivalry between Nigerians and Ghanaians over whose is better is known as the jollof wars.
items.stem: Jollof rice, cooked in a spiced tomato sauce, is a celebrated dish of which region?

items.explanation: Working in Szeged, a paprika-growing city, he found that the local peppers were packed with vitamin C. He received the 1937 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
items.stem: Albert Szent-Györgyi won a Nobel Prize for work on vitamin C, which he extracted in bulk from which Hungarian crop?

items.explanation: It is called a tea, but it is unrelated to the tea plant. Its needle-like leaves turn red as they are bruised and dried in the sun.
items.stem: Rooibos, a caffeine-free red tea, is made from a shrub native to which country?

items.explanation: Its smell is often likened to rotting onions or old socks, yet its sweet, custard-like flesh makes durian a prized treat across Southeast Asia.
items.stem: Which spiky fruit is banned on Singapore's trains because of its powerful smell?

items.explanation: Its relatives include horseradish and mustard. Their heat comes from vapours that rise into the nose, unlike chilli heat, which burns the tongue and lingers.
items.stem: Real wasabi is grated from the stem of a plant in which family?

items.explanation: Cheesemakers once matured it in the caves of Cheddar Gorge. The name travelled with the recipe, and cheddar is made around the world, from Australia to Canada.
items.stem: Which cheese is named after a village in Somerset, south-west England?

items.explanation: Its fame owes much to the Swiss Cheese Union, a cheese-marketing body that promoted fondue as the national dish to sell more cheese.
items.stem: Which Swiss dish is eaten by dipping bread on long forks into a shared pot of melted cheese?

items.explanation: It takes its name from Caesar Cardini, an Italian-born restaurateur usually credited with creating it at his restaurant in Tijuana, Mexico, in the 1920s.
items.stem: The Caesar salad, made with romaine lettuce and Parmesan, is named after Julius Caesar.

items.explanation: Apples cooked in butter and sugar are covered with pastry, baked, then flipped onto a plate. The tart is named after the Tatin sisters, who served it at their hotel in France.
items.stem: Which fruit is used in a classic tarte Tatin, baked upside down under its pastry?

items.explanation: Tiger nuts are small tubers of a sedge, Cyperus esculentus, not nuts at all. Mexican horchata, the version many people know, is usually made with rice.
items.stem: Spain's traditional horchata, a sweet milky drink, is made from which ingredient?

items.explanation: Many familiar citrus fruits descend from a few wild ancestors, chiefly pomelo, mandarin, citron and papeda. Grapefruit later arose in the Caribbean from a pomelo and sweet orange cross.
items.stem: The sweet orange arose as a cross between the pomelo and which other citrus fruit?

items.explanation: The plants were meant to grow cheap food for enslaved workers on British plantations in the Caribbean. Bligh delivered them on a later voyage, and breadfruit became a Jamaican staple.
items.stem: When the crew of HMS Bounty mutinied, the ship was carrying young plants of which food crop from Tahiti?

items.explanation: Sesame pods split open when ripe and scatter their seeds, so farmers cut the plants before the pods burst. Unhulled seeds make a darker, more bitter tahini.
items.stem: Tahini, the paste used in hummus and halva, is made by grinding which seeds?

items.explanation: Gelatin is broken-down collagen, extracted by heating animal tissue in water. Vegetarian versions often use agar, from red seaweed, while jam sets thanks to pectin, found in fruit.
items.stem: Gelatin, which makes gummy sweets (candy) chewy, is usually made from what?

items.explanation: Lebanese families brought spit-roasted lamb, cooked like shawarma, to cities such as Puebla. Mexican cooks swapped in chilli-marinated pork and often crown the spit with a pineapple.
items.stem: Tacos al pastor, carved from a vertical spit, grew out of the cooking of which immigrants to Mexico?

items.explanation: In Germany it is called Schwarzwälder Kirschtorte, and its layers are traditionally soaked in kirsch, a clear cherry brandy from the Black Forest region.
items.stem: Which fruit fills a classic Black Forest gâteau, along with chocolate sponge and cream?

items.explanation: Quinine comes from the bark of the South American cinchona tree. It glows bright blue under ultraviolet light, so tonic water shines under a black light.
items.stem: Which bitter compound, once taken against malaria, gives tonic water its taste?

items.explanation: Avocados do not ripen on the tree, so growers can leave mature fruit hanging for months as natural storage and pick them as needed.
items.stem: Which fruit is mashed to make guacamole?

items.explanation: Appert sealed food in glass bottles and boiled them, winning a French government prize, decades before Pasteur showed that microbes cause spoilage. Nobody yet knew why it worked.
items.stem: Which came first?

items.explanation: Teff grains are about the size of poppy seeds. Diners tear off pieces of injera to scoop up stews, so the bread serves as plate and cutlery at once.
items.stem: Injera, a spongy sourdough flatbread from the Horn of Africa, is traditionally made from which tiny grain?

items.explanation: Purists use young Genovese basil, crushed in a marble mortar with pine nuts, garlic, salt, hard cheese and olive oil.
items.stem: Which herb is the main ingredient of classic Genoese pesto?

items.explanation: The seeds grow in large pods that sprout straight from the tree's trunk and thick branches, a habit botanists call cauliflory.
items.stem: Chocolate is made from the fermented, roasted seeds of which tree?

items.explanation: Scurvy comes from a lack of vitamin C. Dogs and cats make their own, but humans, apes, monkeys and guinea pigs must get it from food.
items.stem: Sailors on long voyages ate citrus fruit to prevent which disease?

items.explanation: Agaves are succulents, not cacti. Growers wait years for each plant to mature, then cut away the leaves and roast the heart, called the piña.
items.stem: Tequila is distilled from which plant?

items.explanation: Green peppercorns are picked unripe and kept green, black ones are unripe berries dried until dark, and white ones are ripe seeds with the skin removed. Pink peppercorns come from a different plant.
items.stem: Black, white and green peppercorns all come from the same plant.

items.explanation: Both are nightshades, like aubergines (eggplants) and chilli peppers. A tomato shoot grafted onto a potato plant can yield tomatoes above ground and potatoes below.
items.stem: Which crop is a close botanical relative of the tomato?

items.explanation: Early ramen shops in Tokyo and Yokohama's Chinatown were run by Chinese cooks, and the dish was long called chuka soba, Chinese soba.
items.stem: Japanese ramen grew out of wheat-noodle soups introduced to Japan by which cooks?

items.explanation: Anna Pavlova toured Australia and New Zealand in the 1920s, and both countries claim the dessert as their own.
items.stem: The meringue dessert pavlova is named after a famous what?

items.explanation: It is also called glutinous rice, yet it contains no gluten. Its stickiness comes from a starch that is almost all amylopectin.
items.stem: Japanese mochi is made by pounding which cooked ingredient into a smooth, stretchy dough?

items.explanation: They are picked by hand before they open, then cured in salt or brine. Left on the bush, a bud becomes a flower and then a caperberry, the plant's fruit.
items.stem: Capers, the small salty green garnish, are which part of a plant?

items.explanation: Mate is often shared from a single gourd among friends in Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay and southern Brazil. Emigrants returning from South America also made it a popular drink in Syria.
items.stem: Which South American drink is sipped from a gourd through a metal straw called a bombilla?

items.explanation: Soaking maize (corn) in alkaline limewater, called nixtamalization, frees the vitamin niacin. Where maize spread without the method, as in parts of Europe, the deficiency disease pellagra followed.
items.stem: Mexican cooks soak which grain in limewater before grinding it into dough for tortillas?

items.explanation: Salt draws water from the shredded cabbage, and microbes already on the leaves sour it naturally, with no vinegar needed. Captain Cook's crews ate it on long voyages.
items.stem: Shredded white cabbage, salted and left to ferment, becomes which German side dish?

items.explanation: The amounts cooks use change the boiling point and the heating time far too little to notice. The fizz when salt hits hot water comes from crystals giving bubbles places to form.
items.stem: Adding salt to a pan of water makes it come to the boil noticeably faster.

items.explanation: Baking soda needs an acid, such as buttermilk or lemon juice, to react. Baking powder carries its own dry acid, so it works with water alone.
items.stem: Which gas do baking soda (bicarbonate of soda) and baking powder release to make cakes rise?

items.explanation: Brewers begin by polishing away the outer layers of each grain. A mould called koji then turns the starch into sugar, which yeast ferments, a process closer to brewing beer than making wine.
items.stem: The Japanese drink sake is brewed from which grain?

items.explanation: Soya (soy) milk is curdled much like cheese, often with nigari, the bitter, mineral-rich liquid left after salt is extracted from seawater.
items.stem: Tofu is made by curdling the milk of which bean and pressing the curds into blocks?

items.explanation: True Neapolitan pizza is baked very quickly in a wood-fired oven, which puffs and chars its soft rim, called the cornicione in Italian.
items.stem: Which Italian city is the home of the pizza Margherita?

items.explanation: Cane sugar was a costly import, sold by apothecaries as a spice and medicine. It became cheap through Caribbean plantations worked by enslaved Africans.
items.stem: Before cane sugar became common, what was the main sweetener in medieval Europe?

items.explanation: Grenade is French for pomegranate, and a pomegranate appears on the coat of arms of Granada, in Spain. Many cheap grenadines swap the fruit for other flavourings.
items.stem: Which fruit gave grenadine syrup its name and its traditional flavour?

items.explanation: Its clear broth simmers for hours with charred onion and ginger, star anise and cinnamon. The dish took shape in northern Vietnam in the early 20th century.
items.stem: Pho, a noodle soup often eaten for breakfast, comes from which cuisine?

items.explanation: It is served with rice, orange slices, sautéed greens and farofa, toasted cassava flour. Its name comes from feijão, the Portuguese word for bean.
items.stem: Feijoada, a slow-cooked stew of black beans and pork, is often called the national dish of which cuisine?

items.explanation: Its name means 'mixed rice', and diners stir everything together before eating. In dolsot bibimbap a sizzling stone bowl gives the rice a crisp crust.
items.stem: Bibimbap, rice topped with vegetables, an egg and chilli paste, comes from which cuisine?

items.explanation: Cooks in Bologna say the thick sauce clings better to flat egg ribbons than to thin spaghetti. The same ragù is layered into the city's green lasagne.
items.stem: In Bologna, the meat sauce ragù alla bolognese is traditionally served with which pasta?

items.explanation: Andalusian farm workers made early gazpachos from bread, oil, vinegar, garlic and water. Tomatoes and peppers, from the Americas, joined the recipe centuries later.
items.stem: Which Spanish soup, made from raw tomatoes, peppers, cucumber, bread and olive oil, is served cold?

items.explanation: Thailand's government promoted the dish in the late 1930s and 1940s, under Prime Minister Plaek Phibunsongkhram, as part of a drive to build a modern national identity.
items.stem: Thailand's pad thai is a stir-fry made with which kind of noodles?

items.explanation: The acid in lime or bitter orange juice unfolds the fish's proteins much as heat does, so the flesh turns firm and opaque within minutes.
items.stem: In ceviche, raw fish is 'cooked' without heat by soaking it in what?

items.explanation: Stones are heated in a fire and laid in a pit, then baskets of meat and vegetables go on top. Everything is covered with cloths and earth and steams for hours.
items.stem: For a Māori hāngī feast in New Zealand, how is the food cooked?
options: In a pit of hot stones

items.explanation: The name comes from the Latin clavus, 'nail', after the bud's shape. Their numbing warmth, once used for toothache, comes from an oil called eugenol.
items.stem: Which spice is the dried, unopened flower bud of a tree from Indonesia's Spice Islands?

items.explanation: Sichuan pepper is the dried husk of a prickly ash berry, unrelated to black pepper. Its sanshool causes the tingle, the 'ma' in the region's mala, numbing and hot.
items.stem: Which Chinese regional cuisine is famous for peppercorns that make the lips tingle and go numb?

items.explanation: Its curds are heated in hot whey, which tightens their proteins and gives the cheese its high melting point. It is traditionally made from sheep's and goat's milk.
items.stem: Halloumi, a cheese firm enough to grill or fry without melting, comes from which island?

items.explanation: Protected rules allow up to 30% goat's milk, with the rest from sheep. The name comes from the Italian fetta, 'slice', after the way it is cut.
items.stem: Traditional Greek feta is made mainly from which animal's milk?

items.explanation: Tamarind trees came from tropical Africa, yet the name comes from the Arabic tamr hindi, 'Indian date', after the sticky brown pulp.
items.stem: Which pod's sour, sticky pulp flavours Worcestershire sauce, south Indian sambar and many chutneys?

items.explanation: Cooks simmer butter until its water boils off and the milk solids brown, then strain them out. Without water or solids, ghee keeps for months and takes higher heat.
items.stem: Ghee, used across South Asian cooking, is a clarified form of what?

items.explanation: Sumac is the dried, ground berry of a shrub that grows wild around the Mediterranean and the Middle East. It adds a lemony sourness to salads such as fattoush.
items.stem: Za'atar, a Middle Eastern seasoning, mixes dried herbs and sesame with which tart, deep-red spice?

items.explanation: Bees pass nectar between them and fan it with their wings until most of its water has evaporated. Finished honey is less than a fifth water, which helps it keep.
items.stem: Honeybees make honey mainly from which part of a flower?

items.explanation: Fresh sap is only about 2% sugar and tastes like faintly sweet water. Producers boil away the rest until the syrup is about two-thirds sugar.
items.stem: About how many litres of maple tree sap are boiled down to make one litre of maple syrup?

items.explanation: Javanese makers mix cooked soya beans with spores of a Rhizopus mould, whose white threads bind the beans into a solid block in a day or two.
items.stem: Tempeh, a firm cake of soya beans knitted together by a mould, comes from which cuisine?

items.explanation: Dried currants are tiny black grapes whose name comes from Corinth in Greece; they are unrelated to blackcurrant bushes. Sultanas are usually pale seedless grapes.
items.stem: Raisins, sultanas and dried currants are all made from which fruit?

items.explanation: The tea bushes are shaded for several weeks before harvest, which deepens their green colour. Drinkers whisk the powder into hot water, so they swallow the whole leaf.
items.stem: Japanese matcha is a fine powder ground from which leaves?

items.explanation: It began as a farmers' breakfast in the canton of Bern. The Röstigraben, or 'rösti ditch', is a joking name for the cultural line between German- and French-speaking Switzerland.
items.stem: Rösti, a crisp golden pancake from Switzerland, is made from grated what?

items.explanation: Olive oil is pressed from the whole fruit rather than from a seed, so it can be eaten fresh without refining. Extra virgin oil is extracted without heat or chemical solvents.
items.stem: Which fruit is pressed to make the oil at the heart of Mediterranean cooking?

items.explanation: Cutting breaks open cells, letting an enzyme called polyphenol oxidase react with oxygen in the air. Lemon juice slows the browning, because its acid holds the enzyme back.
items.stem: What turns the flesh of a freshly cut apple brown?

items.explanation: Salt lowers the freezing point of water, so the melting brine drops well below 0 °C and pulls heat out of the cream fast enough to freeze it.
items.stem: Old hand-cranked ice-cream makers packed the churn in ice mixed with what?

items.explanation: Buttered sheets of filo are layered with chopped nuts such as walnuts or pistachios, baked, then soaked in syrup or honey. Filo comes from the Greek word for leaf.
items.stem: Baklava is built from many paper-thin sheets of which pastry?

items.explanation: Cooks aim for pasta that is cooked through but still offers a slight bite at the centre. Risotto rice is cooked al dente too.
items.stem: Pasta cooked 'al dente' is, word for word, cooked how?

items.explanation: The name refers to its layers: puff pastry, rolled and folded, holds hundreds of butter-thin sheets, and three sheets of it are stacked with pastry cream.
items.stem: The French pastry mille-feuille is named after what?

items.explanation: Wien is the German name for Vienna. The veal is pounded thin, breaded and fried until the crumb coating puffs away from the meat in golden waves.
items.stem: The breaded veal cutlet Wiener schnitzel takes its name from which city?

items.explanation: Cooks curdle hot milk with lemon juice or vinegar, then press the curds. Paneer softens in a curry but does not melt, so its cubes hold their shape.
items.stem: Paneer, used in Indian dishes such as palak paneer, is what kind of food?

items.explanation: Nori sheets are made much like paper: the seaweed is chopped, spread thinly on frames and dried, a method adapted from Japanese papermaking in the Edo period.
items.stem: Which dried seaweed, pressed into thin sheets, is used to wrap sushi rolls?

items.explanation: Peanuts are native to South America. They reached Southeast Asia on Spanish and Portuguese ships in the 16th and 17th centuries and became a staple of the region's cooking.
items.stem: Indonesian and Malaysian satay skewers are usually served with a sauce made from which ingredient?

items.explanation: The aubergines are charred whole over a flame until the skin blackens and the flesh collapses, then mashed with tahini, lemon juice and garlic.
items.stem: Baba ghanoush, a smoky dip from the eastern Mediterranean, is made from which roasted vegetable?

items.explanation: Food is sealed in a vacuum-packed bag, then cooked in a water bath held at an exact temperature, often for hours. French chefs developed the method in the 1970s.
items.stem: The cooking method sous vide takes its name from French words meaning what?

items.explanation: Moroccans brew it with Chinese gunpowder green tea, whose leaves are rolled into tight pellets, and pour it from a height to raise a foam on each glass.
items.stem: Moroccan mint tea is traditionally brewed from fresh spearmint, sugar and which kind of tea?

items.explanation: The white flesh is grated and squeezed with warm water to give a creamy liquid. Coconut water, the clear juice inside young green coconuts, is a different drink.
items.stem: Coconut milk, used in many Thai curries, is made from what?

items.explanation: The 'work' is the main course, so these small dishes stand apart from it. The Italian antipasto, meaning 'before the meal', names the same course another way.
items.stem: Word for word, what does the French term hors d'oeuvre mean?

items.explanation: Portuguese marmelada was a firm paste of marmelos, quinces. In English the word moved to citrus preserves, above all bitter Seville orange marmalade.
items.stem: The word 'marmalade' comes from the Portuguese name of which fruit?

items.explanation: The jar, called a glirarium, had ledges inside for climbing and holes for air. A Roman recipe describes dormice stuffed with pork, pepper and pine nuts, then roasted.
items.stem: Wealthy ancient Romans fattened which small animals in special clay jars to serve at feasts?

items.explanation: Lye, a strong alkali, speeds up browning on the dough's surface. It is caustic, but baking turns it into harmless compounds, leaving the dark, chewy skin.
items.stem: Before baking, German pretzels are dipped briefly in what, which gives them their glossy brown crust?

items.explanation: Working in Java, he saw that chickens fed polished rice developed a similar illness, while those fed whole rice did not. The missing nutrient was vitamin B1, thiamine.
items.stem: Christiaan Eijkman shared a 1929 Nobel Prize after linking the disease beriberi to a diet of what?

items.explanation: Nutmeg is the seed inside the apricot-like fruit of the nutmeg tree, and mace is the lacy red covering, the aril, wrapped around it. Mace turns orange as it dries.
items.stem: The spice nutmeg and the spice mace come from the same fruit.

items.explanation: Staling is mostly starch molecules recrystallizing, not bread drying out, and that happens fastest at fridge temperatures. Freezing stops it, and warming stale bread briefly reverses it.
items.stem: Bread goes stale faster in a fridge than on a kitchen counter.

items.explanation: The story has been told of Henry VIII, James I and Charles II, but the word comes from Old French surloigne: sur, 'above', and loigne, 'loin'.
items.stem: Sirloin steak got its name when an English king knighted a joint of beef as 'Sir Loin'.

items.explanation: Electric toasters were on sale by 1909, so early toast was cut by hand. Machine-sliced bread arrived in 1928 in Chillicothe, Missouri, cut by Otto Rohwedder's slicer.
items.stem: Which came first?

items.explanation: Cacao residues turn up in Central American pottery from about 1500 BC. The earliest reliable evidence of coffee drinking comes from 1400s Yemen, where Sufis drank it to stay awake for night prayers.
items.stem: Which came first?

items.explanation: Espresso is far stronger per sip, but a single shot holds only about 30 ml. A mug of filter coffee is about eight times bigger, so it usually delivers more caffeine overall.
items.stem: Which usually holds more caffeine?

items.explanation: Honey is about four-fifths sugar dissolved in a little water, and all that sugar packs extra mass into every litre, so a litre jar of honey weighs about 1.4 kg.
items.stem: Which is heavier?
